newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market powered ahead at the end on Tuesday, increasing earlier gains, while the long bond future closed above a key resistance at 115.50, fuelling expectations of further advances in the short run.
"Such a strong close fills a gap, and points to further gains," Francisco Esteban, a trader at BNP in Madrid, said.
Dealers said no clear fundamental reason was behind the movement as France's political uncertainty was expected to hang over markets. But bonos shrugged off all uncertainties.
"If anything I would see a reason for a weaker market, not for a stronger one like this," Esteban added.
Dealers said prices were discounting a very high probability for Spain entering in the EMU's first wave.
Earlier on Tuesday Spanish Catalan leader Jordi Pujol said the Bundesbank had a very good impression of Spain's economic trend and of its chances of entering EMU on time.
The 10-year spread over Bunds ended at 66 basis points, not far from its all-time low of 64 basis points hit on Wednesday.
On Wednesday the Spanish Treasury will auction one-year and 18-month bills, whose yields are expected to fall to fresh lows at around five percent for both maturities.
